purpose: Diagnose whether independent causal input excitation improves angular identification before a high-spin forecast.

source.simulator: Crazyflow 0.3.2 through glassbox-throw at source commit 9bd74c1

measurement.excitation: At rows 100 through 149, add amplitude times the four-column Hadamard sign pattern, reversing the sign every four rows, to the recorded issued command and clip each channel to [0,1]. Every eight-row cycle has zero net requested perturbation per channel. No learner state or simulator hidden state selects a perturbation.
measurement.forecast: Fit the public OnlineFit only on the completed branch prefix through row 150. Forecast rows 151 through 175 under the same recorded future issued commands for both amplitudes. Report physical 50, 100 and 250 ms rate errors against branch truth and hold-rate reference.
measurement.response: At row 150, branch the simulator from its exact state and hidden motor condition, perturb one issued command channel by plus/minus 0.05 for one interval, replay the recorded future commands and score the public learner's matched finite-difference 50 and 250 ms body-rate response.
measurement.scope: Controlled simulator diagnosis only. The excited and unexcited branches reach different states; this is not a same-state causal treatment estimate or a Throw controller trial. No simulator hidden state or arm metadata is supplied to Glassbox.
